entries.name: memory_store
entries.description: Store a grounded fact in mem20's persistent memory system. You MUST declare epistemic_status: how this claim came to be known. Use 'observed' only for something you directly witnessed or verified (a command's real output, a file that exists). Use 'inferred' for a conclusion drawn from observations, 'agent_generated' for your own prior claim, 'hypothesis' for a guess, 'user_stated' for something the user told you. If the basis is genuinely unknown use 'unlabeled'. For invented/simulated content use memory_simulate_store instead, which keeps fiction in a separate partition.

Entities are extracted at write time from topics, tags, and proper nouns; returns related entities with hop distance plus the facts that support them. Falls back to partial and substring entity matching. Reports honestly when the graph index has not been built.

entries.description: Report whether the vector, BM25, and graph indexes still agree with the ledger, with exact counts. An index entry whose record no longer exists is a stale pointer: search finds it and then cannot resolve its content. This reports the drift instead of silently returning fewer results.

entries.name: memory_simulate_store
entries.description: Store SIMULATED / imagined content into the SEPARATE simulated partition. This content is NEVER written to grounded memory or the semantic indexes, and cannot be promoted to grounded memory without an explicit confirmation or real-world prediction-error resolution.

entries.name: memory_promote
entries.description: Promote a simulated fact into grounded memory ONLY via an explicit gate: supply a non-empty `confirmation`, or set resolved_via_prediction_error=true with a resolution_note. Otherwise promotion is refused.

entries.name: memory_audit_contamination

entries.name: memory_label_coverage
entries.description: Report how many grounded facts carry an epistemic label and what they say. Answers 'is every stored fact labelled as a fact?' with a number.

entries.name: memory_backfill_labels
entries.description: Mark pre-existing unlabeled grounded facts as 'unlabeled'. Honest, not convenient: their basis cannot be reconstructed, so they are refused by the epistemic veto until a human labels them individually. Never writes 'observed'. Does not modify content, topics, or the simulated partition.

entries.name: irc_status
entries.description: Show the IRC hub: whether each nick is connected and in the channel, and how many protocol lines the noise filter has swallowed. Use this to check the room is reachable before expecting messages, or to confirm a filter is doing its job.

entries.name: irc_join
entries.description: Join the IRC room under a nick and get the backlog depth. The connection is owned by a persistent daemon, so this does not reconnect or lose anything. Returns 'ready', which is true only once the channel roster has arrived and you can actually hear and be heard.

entries.name: irc_read
entries.description: Read channel messages newer than a sequence cursor. Server noise (MOTD, numerics, joins/parts) is already filtered out before it reaches you, so every message here is real conversation. Pass back the 'latest_seq' from the previous call as 'since'. That returns only what arrived since, which is what makes a reply cost one cheap call instead of a re-read of the whole channel. Call once; if it returns nothing new, there is nothing new.

entries.name: irc_say

entries.name: verify_wiring

entries.name: toolchest_inventory
entries.description: Query the mem20 tool registry: every MCP tool, every CLI binary on PATH, and every native mem20 subsystem, with real runtime status. action=list filters by kind/category; action=search matches names and descriptions; action=show returns one entry; action=stats returns counts.

entries.name: toolchest_wiring
entries.description: Prove the tool registry's cross-subsystem edges by calling each one: memory_engine pin_block, mem20kanbanz sha256, mem20ops declared_scripts, mem20corez CharMLP, mem20cliz build_envelope, mem20verify discover_packages. Returns per-edge ok/result so a broken edge is visible, not assumed.
